parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the adult-to-juvenile ratio approached by a non-zero population. Explain why a negative eigenvalue does not mean negative plant numbers.

The negative eigenvalue describes an alternating decaying component; non-negative initial data remain non-negative under $L$.

title: Investment returns with an early exit
stem: An investment costs 5000 now and returns 2000 at the end of each of years 1, 2 and 3. Its net present value at annual rate $r$ is the discounted receipts less 5000. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the net present value at 8% and at 10%.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the annual rate for which the net present value is zero, and explain why there is only one positive solution.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A buyer offers 3500 immediately after the first receipt. At an 8% discount rate, decide whether selling is preferable to retaining the remaining receipts.

steps.text: Each positive receipt decreases as the discount rate increases, so $N$ is strictly decreasing for $r>0$.
At year 1, the remaining receipts have value $2000/1.08+2000/1.08^2$.
This is 3566.53, exceeding 3500; retaining has the higher present value.

title: Reconstructing two original mixtures
stem: A mixing process sends 70% of tank A and 20% of tank B into tank C. The rest enters tank D. Final volumes are 40 litres in C and 60 litres in D. No liquid is lost. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use a matrix inverse to determine the original volumes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Only C is measured with an error: its recorded volume increases by $\varepsilon$ while D stays 60. Find the errors in the recovered volumes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why a much smaller determinant could make this reconstruction less reliable.

steps.text: The determinant is 0.5, so the inverse exists.
Errors are $1.6\varepsilon$ in A and $-0.6\varepsilon$ in B.

For otherwise comparable entries, measurement errors can be magnified substantially.

title: A launch delay avoids a collision
stem: A drone starts at $(0,0)$ with velocity $v_A(t)=(2,2t-2)$. Another drone has position $r_B(t)=(6,t)$, with t in seconds. Coordinates are in metres. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $r_A(t)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether a collision occurs for $t\ge0$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The second drone launches one second later and follows $r_B(t)=(6,t-1)$ for $t\ge1$. Determine whether that avoids collision.

steps.text: Integrate each velocity component and use the initial position.
Thus the drones collide at $(6,3)$ after 3 seconds.
East coordinates can still agree only at $t=3$.
Then A is at $(6,3)$ and B at $(6,2)$, so collision is avoided under this ideal model.

title: Inspecting every road once
stem: A road network has vertices A, B, C and D and the edges shown. A route inspector wants a closed walk that uses each edge exactly once. Edge weights are lengths in kilometres. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: List the degree of each vertex and decide whether the requested walk exists.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Decide whether an open walk using every edge exactly once exists.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why visiting each vertex once is a different problem, and give a valid cycle of that type.

steps.text: Each of A, B, C and D has degree 3.
A connected graph has an Eulerian circuit only when all degrees are even.
The requested closed walk does not exist.
An Eulerian trail with distinct endpoints requires exactly two odd vertices.
There are four odd vertices, so such an open walk also does not exist.
Visiting vertices once is Hamiltonian, while the inspector’s condition concerns edges.
For example A–B–C–D–A visits all vertices once before returning.
